Add encrypted, workspace/project/session-scoped working-set manifests and evidence entries backed by the existing canonical encrypted capture payloads; create stable resume/fork identities, deterministic event eligibility and token estimates, a 100K capacity with diversity-aware non-pinned eviction, pins, tombstones, atomic writes, idempotent replay, source-sequence high-watermarks, degraded states, and deterministic rebuild. Materialize canonical `supermemory.episode.v1` provenance records without duplicating plaintext payloads. Extend `/v1/events` so, only when working memory is explicitly enabled, its acknowledgement truthfully reports working-set/evidence IDs, completeness, durability, capture coverage, and independently verified reopenability after fsync and hash round-trip. Extend the daemon client and capture adapters to preserve those fields and fail open through the existing encrypted spool. Add the Lot 2 offload eligibility/receipt module, but keep actual hook/App Server output replacement disabled for the later Lot 7 canary. Flags disabled must preserve current v1/v2 behavior and create no Working Memory artifacts. Prove rich, standard, partial, duplicate, resume, fork, quota, pin, eviction, tombstone, corruption/rebuild, daemon outage, and post-commit failure behavior without Ollama, Hindsight, Graphiti, Neo4j, credentials, network writes, MCP recall, Active Map, graph, ontology, lifecycle UI, or deployment work.

stop_if: Any required implementation would overwrite, discard, or silently replace existing untracked user work in the approved files instead of merging around it.

A durable or reopen-verified acknowledgement could be returned before the journal, encrypted payload, working evidence, and canonical episode are fsynced and successfully reopened with matching scope and hash.
Working Memory would duplicate full plaintext payloads, expose physical vault paths, weaken redaction/AEAD, or make its projection canonical over the capture journal and Evidence Ledger.
Meeting the 100K quota would require deleting canonical evidence, evicting pinned entries, crossing workspace/session scope, or silently accepting an over-capacity pinned set.
A partial, spooled, timed-out, corrupt, tombstoned, expired, or unverified capture could become offload-eligible or suppress the original Codex result; every degraded path must fail open.
Flags-off/default behavior changes, creates working artifacts, changes existing response semantics, or requires rewriting immutable v1/v2 artifacts.
A required change falls outside allowed_files or enters Active Map/compaction injection, MCP working recall, graph, ontology, improve workers, lifecycle UI, installer/deploy, or production rollout.
Any deterministic test requires Ollama, Hindsight, Graphiti, Neo4j, credentials, a real user vault, or network writes.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.

evidence.findings: Calibration has 15 cases and holdout has 25 disjoint IDs, all final labels, restricted and standard claims, and unique signal vectors. The holdout contains 10 auto, 4 TTL, 7 discard, 3 quarantine, and 1 pending case; its measured auto precision is 100% and standard exception rate is 4.55%. An intentionally imperfect corpus returns mismatches and confusion counts instead of throwing.

`verifyAdmissionDecision` validates schema and TTL semantics, recomputes deterministic admission ID and integrity hash, and accepts expected candidate, workspace, policy, and evidence bindings. Both canonical stores apply those bindings before replay or activation; forged rehashed evidence is rejected by tests.

Automatic `product-store.reviewCandidate` destructures no HTTP verification field and calls `trustedVerification` before admission. The negative API test supplies forged independent signals yet receives `quarantine_resolution_not_verified`, creates no memory, and leaves recall empty.

The sacrificial canary constructs automatic governance, admits through independent verifier metadata, verifies the admission attestation and projection, records `review_candidate_called:false`, and performs cited recall. Codex executable resolution skips unusable candidates and validates the packaged fallback with `--version`.

The local Hindsight test asserts loopback, no writes, no cloud fallback, and explicit blocker codes. It skips only when health/container evidence says unavailable and retains strict localhost/container assertions when present.
Default store, compiler, product server, and CLI modes remain `legacy_manual`; automatic admission requires explicit opt-in. Existing byte-preserved v1 state and legacy manual workflow tests pass.

Focused milestone run: 28 tests, 27 pass and one explicit unavailable Hindsight skip. `npm run verify:codex` passes all nine gates. `npm test` reports 154 tests, 153 pass and the same explicit skip. `npm run verify`, `npm run verify:release`, and `git diff --check` pass.

Lot 2 names the offload module plus daemon client/adapters and requires canonical episodes, extended capture acknowledgements, verified reopening, high-watermarks, degraded state, and fail-open behavior.
